title: QBR Deckset: Mosaic Growth + Risk Ledger
content:
Purpose:
This working doc contains two complementary QBR deck patterns (Standard / Enterprise) plus an embedded renewal tracker ledger and a short operational playbook. The goal is to give CSMs a lightweight, repeatable deck and action flow that can be customized to customer maturity and risk profile.

Notes on audience and usage:
- Use the Standard deck for SMB and mid-market accounts with low technical complexity and a single product line. Keep decks to 10-12 slides, focus on value, adoption, and clear next-step commitments.
- Use the Enterprise deck for strategic accounts with multiple product lines or complex deployments (Dedicated, Private). Expect 15-25 slides; include deeper telemetry, rollout timelines, risk remediation, and exec-level asks.
- This doc is intentionally modular: each slide description includes "core messaging", "speaker notes", and "optional data widgets". CSMs should copy relevant modules into their copy of the deck.

STANDARD DECK PATTERN (10-12 slides) - condensed, outcome-focused
1. Cover + Meeting objectives
   - Core messaging: 30-minute QBR, align on success metrics and renewal health.
   - Speaker notes: Introduce attendees, confirm agenda and timebox.

2. Executive Summary / Health Snapshot (single slide)
   - Core: 3 bullets: ARR at-risk/at-gain, usage velocity, top 1 success metric.
   - Widget: Sparkline for monthly API call volumes.

3. Top Customer Wins (2 bullets)
   - Core: Concrete outcomes (e.g., "reduced inference cost by 21% via batching config").
   - Notes: Tie back to the customer's business KPIs.

4. Adoption + Usage Trends (1-2 slides)
   - Core: Active routes, model variants used, peak latency percentiles.
   - Optional: Small table of top 5 endpoints by token volume.

5. Quality Signals & Incidents (1 slide)
   - Core: Recent incidents, root cause summary, mitigations.
   - Notes: Show SLA impact and current open tickets (link).

6. Cost & Efficiency Opportunities (1 slide)
   - Core: Quick wins (batching, prefix caching, quantization suggestions).
   - Speaker notes: Suggest 1 prioritized experiment for next 30 days.

7. Renewal Health & Ask (1 slide)
   - Core: Renewal likelihood (Green/Amber/Red), proposed commitment, key blockers.
   - Template ask language: "Our recommended renewal path is X. To lock in pricing we need confirmation by DATE."

8. Success Plan / 90-day roadmap (1 slide)
   - Core: 3 milestones with owners and due dates.

9. Risks & Escalation Path (1 slide)
   - Core: Top 3 risks and mitigation owners.

10. Close: Decisions & Next Steps (1 slide)
   - Core: Confirm actions, owners, and dates.

ENTERPRISE DECK PATTERN (15-25 slides) - deep-dive, stakeholder-aligned
1. Cover + Tiered Attendee Map
   - Add a table of attendees, executive sponsor, technical lead, procurement rep.

2. Strategic Context & Business Objectives (1 slide)
   - Link to customer strategy: where Redwood fits into their AI roadmap.

3. Executive Health Dashboard (1 slide, three panels)
   - Financial (ARR / committed usage), Operational (SLOs, error budget), Product (feature adoption).

4. Detailed Usage & Performance (2-3 slides)
   - Token distribution by route, sequence length histograms, P99 latency by region.

5. Security & Compliance Posture (1 slide)
   - If Private/Dedicated: KMS usage, audit log summary, open compliance items.

6. Migration / Rollout Status (1-2 slides)
   - Phased rollout plan (stages, gating criteria, rollback plan).

7. Quality & Evaluation (2 slides)
   - Prompt regression tests, eval suite pass rates, examples of failure modes.

8. Cost Optimization Opportunities (1-2 slides)
   - Simulation of unit economics under alternate configs (e.g., 4-bit quant vs FP16).

9. Contract & Commercial Overview (1 slide)
   - Term, seat/usage tiers, add-ons, pending procurement milestones.

10. Renewal Risk Ledger (explicit table slide)
   - Columns: Risk ID, Category, Impact (ARR), Likelihood, Owner, Mitigation, Due Date, Status.

11. Ask & Executive Decision Map (1 slide)
   - Clear asks split by "Exec -> Approved" / "Tech -> Triage".

12. Appendix: Logs, Ticket links, Eval artifacts (multiple slides)

RENEWAL TRACKER LEDGER (embedded template)
- This is meant to be copy/pasted into the deck or maintained as a live sheet. Fields:
  * customer_name
  * renewal_date
  * contract_value (ARR)
  * current_commitment_status (Committed / Negotiating / At-risk)
  * renewal_owner (CSM)
  * exec_sponsor_confirmed (yes/no)
  * top_risks (short list)
  * next_ask (pricing / exec meeting / pilot)
  * last_touch_date
  * next_touch_date
  * jira_link_to_open_issues

Sample rows (text table)
| customer_name | renewal_date | ARR | status | owner | exec_sponsor | next_ask | next_touch |
| Acme Retail   | 2026-02-15   | $320k | Negotiating | A. Patel | Yes | Price lock + dedicated baseline | 2025-10-22 |
| FinNova       | 2025-12-01   | $1.2M | At-risk    | D. Martinez | No  | Exec executive sync | 2025-10-18 |

PLAYBOOK: PRE, DURING, POST QBR (operational checklist)
Pre-QBR (2-3 weeks out)
- Confirm attendees and roles; send pre-read 7 days prior.
- Run data pulls: last 90 days of routes, latency percentiles, cost delta per route.
- Identify 1-2 quantitative wins to highlight (cost saved, latency improved).
- Create tailored asks: example ask templates included at bottom.

During QBR (timeboxed)
- Start with 5-min exec summary. Keep the rest of the meeting structured around decisions.
- Use visuals: one chart per slide, avoid dense tables.
- Where there is a live issue, pull up ticket and proposed remediation with owner.

Post QBR (24-72 hrs)
- Send meeting notes with actions in a tracker and link to the renewal ledger.
- Create follow-up tasks in Jira and assign owners.
- Update renewal probability status and notify RevOps for forecasting.

Decision language templates (copy+paste)
- Low friction ask: "To secure the rate for the next 12 months we need written confirmation by {DATE}. If agreeable, please reply with 'Approve' and we'll send the updated SOW."
- Exec escalation ask: "We recommend an executive alignment call to approve the proposed usage baseline and procurement timeline. Suggested attendees: {list}. Proposed dates: {3 choices}."

Risk signals and play actions
- Usage plateau for two consecutive quarters -> Action: propose adoption sprint, assign Solutions Eng, schedule a health-check workshop.
- Major incident impacting latency > 2 hours -> Action: open severity ticket, propose joint RCA within 72 hours, schedule executive notification.
- Procurement stalls (no PO after 30 days) -> Action: escalate to sales AE and RevOps; prepare alternate contract language for interim consumption.

Appendix: quick data queries & screenshot guidance
- API metrics query (sample): SELECT route, count(*) as calls, avg(latency_p50) FROM request_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '90 days' GROUP BY route ORDER BY calls DESC LIMIT 10;
- Screenshot checklist: include chart title, time-range, and axis labels; annotate spikes with likely cause.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Build a 1-page one-click export from CS console that populates the renewal ledger above.
- Decide final thresholds for green/amber/red renewal scoring and add to RevOps forecast sync.
- Get buy-in on enterprise deck appendix format from Solutions Eng.

Attachments to create next iteration:
- One-pager "QBR quick-start checklist" (printable)
- A slide pack of 6 one-liner 'asks' for execs (pre-approved wording)
- Excel/Sheet template for automated renewal ledger (with example formulae)

Contact / owner note:
- Owner: Asha Patel (CS Lead, Enterprise programs)
- For playbook changes ping #cs-qbr in Slack, link back to Confluence index above.

This is a working draft — please add comments inline and flag any mandatory commercial/legal language to include before we roll the Enterprise version to the full CS team.
